findings.headline: Durham's surveyed population grew from 317,886 in 1986 to 691,893 in 2022 (118%).
findings.notes: Household survey population estimates, all ages.

findings.headline: Working at home went from 4.9% of employed residents in 1991 to 14.1% in 2022.
findings.notes: Full-time + part-time usually-work-at-home as a share of employed persons. 1986 is not computable from the published cells (the part-time-at-home cell is suppressed, affecting numerator and denominator), so the series starts in 1991. 2022 reflects post-2020 hybrid work.

findings.headline: The average Durham household owned 1.71 vehicles in 1986; in the 2022 survey it owned 1.81.
findings.notes: Top-coded '5 or more' counted as 5, so means are slightly low; the bias need not be identical across communities.

findings.headline: Transit share of weekday trips: highest Ajax (5.0%), lowest Uxbridge (0.5%).
findings.notes: Share of resident weekday trips by local transit + GO (2022).

findings.headline: Households with no vehicle: highest Oshawa (8.1%), lowest Clarington (2.9%).
findings.notes: Share of households reporting zero vehicles (2022).

findings.headline: Walking share of weekday trips: highest Ajax (10.6%), lowest Scugog (5.4%).
findings.notes: Share of resident weekday trips on foot (2022).

findings.headline: Workers commuting to Toronto: highest Pickering (37.0%), lowest Scugog (9.4%).
findings.notes: Employed residents whose usual workplace is in Toronto, as a share of all employed residents (2022). The stricter usual-workplace denominator is never complete (suppressed area cells), so employed residents is the denominator.

findings.headline: Vehicles per household: highest Uxbridge (2.10), lowest Oshawa (1.60).
findings.notes: Mean vehicles per household (2022), top-coded at 5.

findings.headline: 64.6% of weekday trips by Durham residents are made as the driver of a private car; 83.2% are made by car, driving or riding.
findings.value: auto driver 64.6%, passenger 18.5%, transit 3.5%, walk 8.3%, bike 0.7%, school bus 3.7%, other 0.6%
findings.notes: 2022 methodology (persons 5+, fuller walking capture). Shares may not sum to 100% due to rounding.

findings.headline: Transit's share of resident weekday trips moved from 4.6% in 1991 to 6.4% in 2016 (comparable 11+ cycles only).
findings.notes: 1991–2016 only: 1986 collected trips at ages 6+ and 2022 at ages 5+ with fuller walking capture — both are excluded as different bases.

findings.headline: Ward-level transit share ranges from 5.1% in Oshawa Ward 2 to 0.2% in Scugog Ward 4.
findings.notes: Wards with ≥500 surveyed households; suppressed shares excluded.
